intro: Pick components by what the product has to do, not by what looks nice. Each playbook lists the usual needs of a domain, the opendraft components and blocks that serve each one, and how well they fit: ready (use as is), adapt (works with the caveat given) or gap (nothing fits yet; build it from primitives and follow the domain principles).

domains.title: Security and compliance
domains.summary: Security operations, threat detection, access control and audit products. Used by analysts under pressure: dense data, fast triage, irreversible actions.
principles: Never show severity by color alone. Pair every severity color with a text label (Critical, High, Medium, Low) and use the same scale everywhere.
Show times as absolute UTC in `font-mono` with a relative hint (for example `14:02:09Z · 3 min ago`). Analysts compare timestamps across systems.
Make destructive or far-reaching actions (isolate a host, revoke a session, delete a key) require confirmation that names the consequence, and show who did it and when afterward.
Mask secrets by default (tokens, keys, hashes) with an explicit reveal and a `copy-button`. Never log or echo them.
Favor dense, keyboard-first tables and a `command-palette` for jumping to an entity. Default these products to the dark theme, but keep both themes working.
Every state change should leave an audit trail the user can see. Plan for an audit-log screen from the start.

needs.notes: Use `badge` variants for severity and status; `table` for large live queues, `filter-table` for filtered lists, `selection-actions` for bulk acknowledge or close.
needs.gap: No four-level severity scale component; map Critical to `destructive`, High and Medium to `warning`, Low to `secondary`, always with text.

needs.need: Investigate an incident: timeline of events and evidence
needs.notes: A vertical `stepper` covers response stages; `code-block` shows raw events.
needs.gap: No timeline or activity-feed component for a chronological event stream.

needs.notes: `approval-card` for an action that needs sign-off, `dialog` with a typed confirmation for the dangerous ones (the settings-page danger zone is the pattern), `sonner` to report the result.
The `settings-page` team section covers invite and role change; `repeater-field` edits rule lists.
needs.gap: No permission-matrix (roles by permissions grid) component.

needs.need: Search and review an audit log
needs.notes: Filters plus `date-range-picker`; show what changed with `diff-table` or `file-diff`.

needs.need: Show security posture and compliance coverage
needs.notes: `analytics-dashboard` takes `labels` and `valueColumn` so it can show findings by severity; `progress` for control coverage.
needs.gap: No gauge or risk-score ring.

needs.need: Sign in with SSO and MFA
needs.notes: `auth-screen` handles email, password and provider buttons.
needs.gap: No one-time-code (OTP) input for MFA.

needs.need: Ask an AI analyst to summarize or investigate
needs.notes: Pass your own conversations and tasks; have the assistant cite evidence with `citations` and ask before acting with `approval-card`.

needs.need: Show assets or attack paths on a map or graph
needs.notes: `flowchart` draws simple flows.
needs.gap: No network graph or geographic map component.

integrations.note: Draw nodes and edges with our tokens for color and type; keep the severity text labels.
Style markers with status tokens and always give each marker a text label for assistive technology.
uPlot copes with very large series; Recharts is quicker to theme.
Put the provider's flow behind the auth-screen block and use otp-input for codes.

domains.title: IT, DevOps and infrastructure
domains.summary: Monitoring, incident management, deployments, logs and internal tools for engineers and IT teams.
principles: Status needs a word and a shape, not just a color: Operational, Degraded, Down, Maintenance. Keep one status vocabulary across the product.
Show times in UTC with `font-mono`, and let the user switch to local time in one place.
Numbers that change should use `tabular-nums` so columns don't jitter; use `animated-number` sparingly on dashboards, never in tables or logs.
Long-running work (deploys, migrations) shows progress, current step and a way to cancel. Never leave a spinner with no step.
Provide a copy button next to every ID, command, hash and URL.
Treat logs and code as data: monospaced, wrap toggle, selectable, searchable.

needs.notes: `stat` tiles with a status `badge` per service; `analytics-dashboard` for the trend.
needs.gap: No status-indicator or uptime-bar component (the 90-day colored bars).

needs.notes: Incident list in a `table`; response steps in `todo-list`.
needs.gap: No timeline component for incident updates.

needs.notes: A virtualized `table` handles very long lists; `code-block` for a single entry.
needs.gap: No log viewer with live tail, level filtering and highlight.

needs.notes: Relabel `analytics-dashboard`; `insight-cards` has chart cards.
needs.gap: No general time-series chart with several series, zoom and thresholds.

needs.notes: Pipeline stages in `flowchart` or a vertical `stepper`; gate a production deploy with `approval-card`; show the change with `file-diff`.
`repeater-field` for key and value rows; mask values and reveal on demand.
needs.gap: No dedicated masked key-value editor.

needs.need: Inventory of servers, services or assets
needs.notes: Virtualized `table` for thousands of rows; `records-table` for editable records.
`command-palette` for actions; `code-panel` for output.
needs.gap: No real terminal emulator.

needs.notes: Pass the real workspace name, members and billing.
Ask for approval before any action that changes production.

integrations.note: Wrap the chart so colors come from CSS variables, and show a table fallback for accessibility.
The Table is already virtualized; for millions of lines the work belongs server-side.
Use flowchart for simple flows and a graph library when users must pan, zoom and edit.
Update rows in place and highlight what changed without moving the layout under the cursor.

domains.title: Aviation and travel operations
domains.summary: Airline and airport operations, flight information, booking and check-in, crew and maintenance tools. Safety-critical context: clarity and correctness beat flourish.
principles: State times with an explicit zone. Use 24-hour time, mark UTC as `Z`, and show the airport's local time beside it. Never leave a time ambiguous.
Flight status is always a word first (On time, Delayed, Boarding, Departed, Cancelled) with a color second. Show the reason and the new time for any delay.
Use IATA or ICAO codes in `font-mono` with the full name on hover or beneath, for example `LIS` and Lisbon.
On safety-critical screens (maintenance sign-off, checklists, weather) turn motion off, show who signed and when, and require an explicit confirm. Prefer `approval-card` over a quiet toggle.
Design for tablets, gloves and bright light: large touch targets, high contrast, no hover-only information.
A live board updates in place without shifting the layout under a user's cursor. Highlight what changed, then settle.

needs.notes: A virtualized `table` with a status `badge`; `text-scramble` can animate a changed gate or time.
needs.gap: No split-flap display.

needs.notes: A vertical `stepper` for legs and connections; `progress` for the flight's progress.
needs.gap: No route or flight-path map.

needs.notes: `catalog` can list fares if you relabel it and pass `layout="compact"`; passengers with `quantity-stepper`.
needs.gap: No origin and destination airport picker, and no fare comparison grid.

needs.notes: `checkout` is a three-step flow; pass your own labels and `ticketFields`.
`ticket-pass` with gate, seat and boarding group as `fields`. The QR is real, but airlines encode a standard barcode (PDF417 or Aztec) that `qr-code` does not produce.
needs.gap: No PDF417 or Aztec barcode.

needs.notes: Nothing fits.
needs.gap: No seat map.

needs.notes: A table works for lists of duties.
needs.gap: No scheduler, Gantt or calendar timeline.

needs.notes: Each item signed with `approval-card`; keep the record in `records-table` with who and when.
On-time performance and disruption counts in `stat` tiles.
needs.gap: No map and no alert banner for weather or NOTAM bulletins.

integrations.note: Great-circle arcs and tracks are a map-library job; keep times and codes in the table beside it.
Normalize to UTC and show local airport time beside it.
qr-code only draws QR; airlines use PDF417 or Aztec, which these libraries can render.
Until a scheduler exists in opendraft, embed one and theme it with the CSS variables.

domains.title: Logistics, supply chain and fleet
domains.summary: Shipment tracking, dispatch, warehouse and fleet products for operators, drivers and customers who need to know where things are and when they'll arrive.
principles: Every shipment shows three things at a glance: status (as a word), where it is, and when it will arrive (an ETA with a confidence or a delay reason).
Tracking IDs, container numbers and SKUs go in `font-mono` with a `copy-button`.
Exceptions come first: delayed, held and failed deliveries sort to the top and carry the reason and the next action.
Show dates and times in the location's own time zone, and say which zone.
Operators work in bulk: every list needs multi-select with bulk actions (`selection-actions`), saved filters and keyboard navigation.
Driver and warehouse screens are used one-handed on a phone: large targets, one primary action per screen, works on a poor connection.

needs.notes: A vertical `stepper` for milestones; `progress` for the journey; show the tracking ID with `copy-button`.
needs.gap: No timeline with timestamps and locations per event, and no route map.

needs.need: Manage a list of shipments or orders
needs.notes: Tabs for Exceptions, In transit and Delivered; a virtualized `table` when volumes are large.
`crm-pipeline` is a stage board with drag and drop; pass your stages (Unassigned, Assigned, En route, Delivered) and relabel the cards.
needs.gap: Its data shape is sales-oriented (company, value, contact); there is no generic board.

needs.notes: A wizard with `stepper`; packages as rows in `repeater-field`; finish with `order-confirmation`.
Utilization and on-time rate in `stat`; driver list in `table`.
needs.gap: No live map of vehicle positions.

needs.notes: Zones as `progress` bars with a warning tone when nearly full.
needs.gap: No barcode scan input and no heat map of locations.

needs.notes: A confirmation step with `approval-card` and a recipient `field` works.
needs.gap: No signature pad and no photo capture or file dropzone.

needs.notes: `checkout` summary pattern for a quote; invoices in `table`.
needs.gap: No dedicated quote or rate-comparison table.

needs.notes: Relabel the dashboard (shipments, on-time rate, cost per delivery) and add a `valueColumn` for cost.
needs.gap: The range tabs are fixed at 7, 30 and 90 days, and the table columns are page-analytics shaped.

integrations.note: Use a map library for positions and routes; keep ETA and status in opendraft components.
Map each carrier's status codes to one status vocabulary before it reaches the UI.
Scanning is a device capability; opendraft's qr-code only generates codes.
Pair with dropzone for photos to make proof of delivery.

domains.title: Healthcare and patient care
domains.summary: Clinical and patient-facing health products: EHR views, scheduling, telehealth and patient portals. Clinicians work under time pressure with safety-critical data; patients need calm, plain-language screens.
principles: Show patient identity on every clinical screen: full name, date of birth and an identifier in `font-mono`, pinned in a header that never scrolls away. Wrong-patient errors are the failure to design against.

Always print units and reference ranges beside a measurement (`5.4 mmol/L, ref 3.9 to 5.6`), and never round or reformat a value without saying so. Do not rely on color alone to mark an abnormal or critical value; pair it with a text flag such as High, Low or Critical.

Critical values and allergy warnings stay visible until a named user acknowledges them. Never auto-dismiss a clinical alert or put one in a toast; use a persistent `alert` and record who acknowledged it and when.
Privacy by default: mask identifiers and sensitive fields until revealed, keep reveals logged, and avoid showing patient names in browser titles, notifications and URLs.
Write patient-facing copy in plain language at a low reading level, explain medical terms in place, and say what happens next. Lead with the answer (`Your results are normal`), not the data.

Confirm irreversible or high-risk actions (sign an order, discharge, cancel a procedure) in a `dialog` that names the patient and the consequence. Where regulation applies, keep an audit trail of who viewed or changed a record.

needs.notes: `page-header` plus `avatar` and `badge` for name, age and flags; `stat` tiles for latest vitals; `tabs` for Summary, Orders, Notes and Results; a persistent `alert` for allergies.
needs.gap: No dedicated pinned patient-banner component; build it from page-header and badge and keep it sticky.

needs.need: Lab results and vitals with abnormal flags
needs.notes: `table` with a value, unit, range and a text-labelled `badge` per row; `stat` for the latest reading.
needs.gap: No time-series chart for trends of a vital or lab value over time (with reference-range band) and no sparkline.

needs.notes: `alert` is persistent and severity-aware; require acknowledgement with `approval-card` or a `dialog` and keep who and when. Do not use `sonner` for clinical alerts.
`stepper` for reason, clinician, time and confirm; `radio-group` for time slots; `order-confirmation` can confirm the booking if relabelled.
needs.gap: No calendar or day/week schedule view and no slot-grid component; clinic staff schedules need a scheduler.

needs.notes: Active medications in a `table` with dose, route and frequency columns; sign orders with `approval-card`; `repeater-field` edits multi-line prescriptions.
needs.gap: No drug-interaction or dose-check UI; this comes from your clinical decision support service and needs a custom alert.

needs.notes: Controls (mute, camera, leave) can be buttons and a waiting-room status can be a `badge`.
needs.gap: No video call surface or device check; embed a video SDK and build the tile grid yourself.

needs.notes: `stepper` splits a long form into short steps; `dropzone` accepts insurance card and ID photos.
needs.gap: No signature pad for consent and no rich text editor for notes.

needs.notes: `timeline` for encounters and events, `todo-list` for care-plan tasks, `progress` for goal tracking.

needs.need: Secure messaging with the care team
needs.notes: The chat components give threads, bubbles and an input; show a clear note that messages are not for emergencies.
needs.gap: No attachment preview, read receipts or clinician-routing; add them and keep the thread data on your own secure backend.

needs.need: Sign in with MFA and a proxy or caregiver
needs.notes: `auth-screen` for sign in, `otp-input` for the verification code; caregiver access can sit in the `settings-page` team section relabelled.

integrations.note: opendraft is presentation only; map FHIR resources to the props of `table`, `stat` and `timeline` in a thin adapter and keep PHI out of client logs.
The SDK renders the video; use opendraft buttons, badges and `alert` for controls, waiting-room state and connection warnings around it.
No time-series chart ships yet; style the chart with the `--blue-*` and semantic tokens and draw the reference range as a shaded band with a text legend.
Use for clinician schedules; keep opendraft `date-picker` and `radio-group` for the patient-facing booking path.
No signature pad is included; capture the signature as an image and store it with a timestamp and the consent text version.

domains.title: Fintech and banking
domains.summary: Banking, payments, trading, personal finance and lending products. Money moves, so precision, clear fees and honest balances matter more than delight; many actions cannot be undone.
principles: Format money with the locale and ISO 4217 currency (`Intl.NumberFormat`), show the currency on every amount that might be ambiguous, align figures right in `tabular-nums` and keep minor units. Never compute with floating point; use integer minor units or a decimal library.

Treat transfers, payouts and trades as irreversible: show a review step with payee, amount, fee, rate and arrival time, then confirm. Require step-up authentication (a one-time code or biometric) before a high-risk action.
Show every fee, rate and the final total before the user commits, not after. If the amount can change (FX, market orders), say so and show when the quote expires.
Be honest about balance: label Available versus Pending versus Current, show `as of` time, and mark data that is delayed. Never show an optimistic balance as if it had settled.
Never use red and green alone for gain and loss; add a sign and an arrow or word (`+2.4%`, `Down`). Do not use red for a number that is merely negative in an accounting sense when it is not an error.

Keep an audit trail the user can see (activity, statements, who approved what) and mask account and card numbers by default, showing only the last four digits with an explicit reveal and `copy-button`.

needs.notes: `stat` tiles for each account with an `as of` hint; use `animated-number` only on a hero balance, never inside tables. Pass formatted strings so the currency is exact.
Status `badge` for Pending, Posted and Failed; virtualized `table` for long histories; export through `selection-actions`.

needs.need: Send money / transfer with review and step-up auth
needs.notes: A `stepper` flow: payee, amount, review, `otp-input` for step-up, then `order-confirmation` as the receipt. Use `approval-card` to show the full fee and amount summary.
`checkout` has a masked card form and a summary, and it never sends full card data to your code; mount your provider's hosted fields in its place.
needs.gap: Its details step is shaped for ticket purchases (attendee, delivery); relabel or build a plain payment form from `field` for bank products.

needs.notes: Holdings in a `table` with signed change values; relabel `analytics-dashboard` for portfolio performance.
needs.gap: No price chart (candlestick or line with ranges and crosshair), no order book and no live ticker; use a charting library and keep numbers in tabular figures.

needs.notes: `tabs` for Buy and Sell, `quantity-stepper` for units, an `approval-card` for the order preview with estimated cost and fees.
needs.gap: No market-depth or order-ticket component; the estimated price must come from your pricing service and show when it was quoted.

needs.notes: `progress` with a warning tone for category budgets; `insight-cards` for monthly trends.
needs.gap: No donut or category-breakdown chart and no cash-flow (Sankey) chart.

needs.notes: `slider` for amount and term, a live repayment summary in `stat`, `dropzone` for income documents.
needs.gap: No amortization schedule table with built-in calculations; compute it server-side and render it with `table`.

needs.notes: `stepper` with a clear status for each check (Pending, Verified, Needs attention) and `dropzone` for ID upload.
needs.gap: No camera capture or liveness-check UI; use your identity provider's SDK.

needs.notes: Card freeze and limits as `switch` and `field`, device and login history in a `table` or `timeline`, a type-to-confirm `dialog` for closing an account.

integrations.note: Mount the provider's hosted fields in place of the `checkout` card inputs so card data never touches your app; opendraft's `onPay` should receive a token only.

integrations.for: Bank account linking and open banking data
integrations.note: These open their own modal; surround it with an opendraft `dialog` that explains what is shared and wait for the result before updating balances.
Pass already formatted strings to `stat` and `table`; keep amounts in integer minor units in your data layer.
No price chart ships in opendraft; theme the chart with design tokens and add a text value readout so gain and loss do not rely on color.
Use their SDK for document and liveness capture and show the outcome with `status-indicator` and `alert`.

domains.title: E-commerce and marketplaces
domains.summary: Storefronts, marketplaces and seller dashboards. Shoppers need honest prices and stock and a fast path to pay; sellers need to manage orders and inventory in bulk.
principles: Be honest about price and availability: show the total with tax, shipping and fees before checkout, strike through a compare-at price only when it is real, and show stock states in words (In stock, Only 3 left, Sold out) from live data.
Persist the cart across sessions and devices, never silently change a quantity or price, and if something changed since the user added it, say what changed and let them decide.

Show trust signals where the decision happens: delivery date, return window, secure payment note, ratings with the review count and who can leave a review. Do not invent urgency such as fake countdowns.
Offer guest checkout and fast payment options; ask for the fewest fields, validate inline and keep the order summary visible while the user fills the form.
State returns, refunds and shipping costs in plain words before purchase, and give the order status and the next step on every order screen.
Make sold-out and error states useful: offer a back-in-stock notification or similar items, keep filters on a no-results page and keep the user's progress when a payment fails.

needs.notes: `catalog` already has search, category chips, sort, price filter, availability switch, card grid, empty state and loading skeleton, with an ISO `currency` prop.
needs.gap: Its item shape is event-oriented (host, date, capacity, remaining) so product fields like brand, variants and ratings need relabelling or a custom card; there are no faceted multi-filters such as size or color.

needs.need: Product detail with variants and purchase panel
needs.notes: `detail-page` has media, key facts, tabs, FAQ, a sticky purchase panel with tiers, quantity and a running total; map tiers to variants or sizes.
needs.gap: No image gallery or zoom, no color swatches and no star rating or review list.

needs.notes: A cart in a `drawer` with `quantity-stepper` lines and a subtotal; the `checkout` summary has the same pattern.
needs.gap: No standalone cart component; build the line list yourself and keep it in persistent storage on your backend.

needs.notes: `checkout` is a three-step flow with a sticky order summary, quantity steppers, discount codes and a masked card form; pass `items`, `fees`, `currency` and `discountCodes`.
needs.gap: Its details step is ticket-shaped (attendee, email or desk delivery); there is no shipping address form, shipping-method picker or wallet-button slot, so add those with `field` and `radio-group`.

needs.notes: `order-confirmation` for the receipt (relabel for physical goods); `stepper` or `timeline` for Placed, Packed, Shipped and Delivered with a tracking number and `copy-button`.
A `stepper` flow: select items, reason, photos with `dropzone`, then choose refund or exchange and confirm; show the return deadline in an `alert`.
needs.gap: No printable return-label view; render it from your carrier's PDF.

needs.notes: Relabel `analytics-dashboard` for revenue, orders and conversion, with `valueColumn` for revenue.
needs.gap: The range tabs are fixed at 7, 30 and 90 days and the table columns are page-analytics shaped; no time-series chart with comparison.

needs.notes: Tabs for New, To ship and Returns, bulk label and fulfil via `selection-actions`, `progress` with `invert` for stock levels.

needs.need: Create and edit a product listing
needs.notes: `repeater-field` for variants and prices, `dropzone` for photos.
needs.gap: No rich text editor for descriptions and no image reordering or cropping.

needs.notes: A `table` of codes with a status `badge`, a `dialog` to create one, and `date-range-picker` for the validity window.

integrations.note: Map the product, cart and order objects to the props of `catalog`, `detail-page` and `checkout` in an adapter; keep the cart on the server so it persists across devices.
Mount hosted card fields in place of the `checkout` card inputs; `onPay` should receive a token, and tax should come from the provider so the total shown is the total charged.
Feed results into `catalog` through its items prop; faceted filters beyond price and category are not built in and need your own controls.
Use their rates in the checkout `fees` and their tracking events in a `timeline`.
No rating component ships in opendraft; show the average and count as plain text next to the stars, and avoid displaying reviews you cannot verify.

domains.title: Education and learning
domains.summary: Learning platforms, courses, classrooms and student information systems. Learners need to know where they are and what is next; instructors need to see a whole class at a glance and act in bulk.
principles: Make progress visible everywhere: where the learner is in the course, what is done, what is next and how long it takes. Use `progress` and `stepper` with text (`3 of 8 lessons`), and always offer a clear Continue action.

Accessibility first: sufficient contrast, full keyboard use, captions and transcripts for media, readable text sizes, no time limits that cannot be extended, and no meaning by color alone. Learners often use shared, older or assistive devices.

Give low-pressure feedback: say what was right and what to try next, avoid red-X shaming, let learners retry, and show a grade only when the instructor chooses to release it. Celebrate completion without confetti that cannot be turned off.

Separate instructor and learner views: the same course shows authoring, grading and class analytics to instructors, and only the learner's own work and progress to students. Never expose other students' names or grades.
Be offline-tolerant: save drafts and answers locally as the learner types, show a visible Saved or Not saved state, and queue submissions with a clear status when the connection drops.

Protect minors' data: avoid public profiles by default, show only what a guardian or teacher needs, and put sensitive records behind explicit access. Where regulation applies, keep consent and access records.

needs.notes: `catalog` for browsing with search, categories and sort; `detail-page` has schedule, FAQ, tiers and seats left, which maps to course sessions and cohorts.
needs.gap: Item fields are event-shaped (host, date, capacity) so relabel them for instructor, start date and seats; no prerequisite or level filters.

needs.notes: `progress` per course with a Continue button, `stat` for streak or time spent, `empty-state` for a new learner.
Modules in an `accordion` or `sidebar-nav`, a vertical `stepper` for the lesson path, with a done or locked state per item.
Transcript, notes and resources can sit in `tabs`; `code-block` for programming lessons.
needs.gap: No video player with captions, speed control and resume, and no PDF or slide viewer; embed one and keep the transcript beside it.

needs.notes: `question-card` presents a question with options; `radio-group` and `checkbox` for answers; `progress` shows question count; a `dialog` confirms submit and names unanswered questions.
needs.gap: No timer with accessibility extensions, no question-bank authoring and no automatic scoring or explanations view.

needs.notes: `dropzone` for uploads, a status `badge` (Not started, Submitted, Late, Graded), `timeline` for submission history; an `alert` for the deadline.
A class-by-assignment `table` with bulk actions; `records-table` for editable rows; `textarea` for feedback and `slider` for a rubric score.
needs.gap: No sticky-header spreadsheet grid with inline editing, and no rubric component.

needs.notes: Relabel `analytics-dashboard` for completion and engagement; `progress` for each assignment's completion.
needs.gap: No time-series or distribution chart (grade histogram) and no per-student drill-down chart.

needs.notes: A `timeline` or `table` can list upcoming deadlines in order.
needs.gap: No calendar or week-view timetable.

needs.notes: The chat and agent components give threads and an input; `citations` lets a tutor point to course material.
needs.gap: No threaded forum with replies and moderation; label AI answers clearly and let the instructor review them.

integrations.note: No video player ships in opendraft; embed one with captions and playback speed, report progress back to update `progress`, and place the transcript in `tabs` beside it.
These sit in your backend; opendraft only renders the resulting course, grade and progress data, so map them into the props of `progress`, `table` and `stepper`.

integrations.for: Rostering and sign-in with school accounts
integrations.note: Use `auth-screen` with their provider buttons; keep the roles (student, teacher, guardian) in your own data so views can differ.
Save answers and drafts locally and show a Saved or Queued state with `badge`; flush the queue on reconnect.
No calendar component ships yet; use it for the week view and keep the opendraft `timeline` for a simple upcoming-deadlines list.

domains.title: Energy, utilities and EV charging
domains.summary: Grid operations, smart metering, solar and storage, EV charging networks, field service and customer billing for electricity, gas and water providers. Numbers carry units, time carries a zone, and some actions can hurt people or equipment.
principles: Always show the unit and the magnitude together, in `font-mono` with `tabular-nums`: `4.2 kW`, `18.6 MWh`, `230 V`. Do not auto-switch between W, kW and MW inside one column; pick one unit per column and say it in the header.

Be honest about time series. Label the interval and aggregation (15-min average, hourly sum, daily peak), mark gaps and estimated reads as such instead of drawing a line through them, and never smooth data without saying so.

Outage and alarm severity uses a fixed scale with a word and an icon, not color alone (for example Critical, Major, Minor, Advisory). Show start time, affected customers or assets, and estimated restoration time with its source.

Switching, isolating or energizing equipment is guarded by interlocks: show the current state, the precondition that blocks the action, and require a confirmation that names the asset and consequence. Show who did it and when, and never allow a one-click remote switch.

Show every timestamp with its zone, and show the asset's own local time beside the operator's. Grids span regions, and daylight saving shifts create 23- and 25-hour days; billing periods and tariffs must follow the meter's zone.
Separate measured, estimated and forecast values visually and in text (solid, dashed, labeled). A billing or settlement figure always shows its status: actual, estimated or disputed.

needs.notes: `stat` tiles for load, generation and frequency with the unit inside `value`; `status-indicator` plus a text `badge` per substation or feeder; `alert` for active network notices.
needs.gap: `stat` has a change chip but no threshold or limit marking, and there is no single-line diagram or network topology view.

needs.need: Live and historical load, generation and consumption charts
needs.notes: `analytics-dashboard` and `insight-cards` can show a trend and totals for a coarse range.
needs.gap: No general time-series chart with several series, units on two axes, zoom, thresholds, gap rendering and forecast overlays.

needs.notes: Virtualized `table` with sortable columns, a meter ID in `font-mono` with `copy-button`, read quality shown as a text `badge` (Actual, Estimated, Missing), and `selection-actions` for bulk reads or commands.
Outage list in `table` with severity `badge`; each outage's updates in `timeline`; restoration stages (reported, crew dispatched, repair, restored) in a vertical `stepper`.
needs.gap: No outage map and no affected-area polygon view.

needs.need: EV charging network and charge point status
needs.notes: Charge points in `table` with connector status words (Available, Charging, Faulted, Offline); `progress` with `invert` for session state of charge; `stat` for uptime and energy delivered.
needs.gap: No station map, and `filter-table` is task shaped (todo, progress, done) so use `table` with your own filter controls for charger statuses.

needs.need: Start and monitor a charging session (driver)
needs.notes: Scan or enter a charger code, show `progress` for charge level, `stat` for kWh, cost and time remaining, and a clear stop `button`. Use `alert` for a faulted connector.
needs.gap: No QR scanner (`qr-code` only renders codes) and no payment-method selector built for tap-to-pay.

needs.notes: Production, consumption, export and battery level in `stat` and `progress` (use `invert` so a low battery warns); `slider` and `switch` for reserve level and backup mode.
needs.gap: No energy-flow diagram (solar to home to battery to grid) and no multi-series time-series chart.

needs.need: Field service work orders and technician dispatch
needs.notes: Work orders in `table`; job detail in `detail-page`; safety and completion checklist in `todo-list` with sign-off through `approval-card`; photo evidence through `dropzone`.
needs.gap: No scheduler or map-based dispatch board, no signature pad, and offline sync of work orders is your app's job.

needs.notes: Bill summary in `stat`, line items in `table`, budget used in `progress` (consumption tone), payment through `checkout`, receipts through `order-confirmation`.
needs.gap: No usage-versus-tariff-band chart (time-of-use bands) and no bill document viewer; render the PDF with an external viewer.

needs.need: Demand response, switching and control actions
needs.notes: Use `dialog` with a typed asset name for switching or load shedding, `approval-card` for two-person sign-off, `sonner` for the result, and `timeline` for who did what and when. Interlock rules and permissions still come from your control system.

integrations.for: Time-series charts for load, generation and meter data
integrations.note: opendraft has no general time-series chart yet; theme the library with opendraft's color tokens, and use uPlot or ECharts when you plot tens of thousands of interval reads.

integrations.for: Maps of outages, substations, feeders and charge points
integrations.note: Put the map beside a `table` or `drawer` from opendraft and encode severity with shape and label as well as color, since map tiles change the contrast.
Stream into `table` and `stat` and keep the last-update time visible; show a stale state when the feed drops rather than the last value as if it were current.

integrations.for: Time zones, daylight saving and interval math
integrations.note: Do billing and interval aggregation in the meter's zone, and format with the zone abbreviation next to `font-mono` timestamps.

integrations.for: Payments for charging sessions and bills
integrations.note: Pair with `checkout` for the form layout and let the provider's hosted fields handle card data.

integrations.for: Barcode and QR scanning for meters, chargers and assets
integrations.note: opendraft's `qr-code` only draws codes; add a scanner component and show a manual-entry `field` as the fallback.

domains.title: Government and civic services
domains.summary: Public-sector portals for permits, licences, benefits, tax, records requests, case management and civic engagement. Used by everyone, including people in stress, on old phones and with assistive technology, so clarity and access come before polish.
principles: Write in plain language: short sentences, common words, one idea per paragraph, the action in the button label (`Apply for a parking permit`, not `Submit`). Explain any term of art the first time it appears.

Design to a high accessibility bar (aim for WCAG 2.2 AA or better, where regulation applies it is often required): visible focus, 4.5:1 text contrast, full keyboard use, errors announced and linked to their fields, no information by color alone, and a tested screen reader path for every form.

Long forms must be save-and-resume: ask one thing per step, show the steps with a `stepper`, let people leave and return with a reference number, never lose entered data on an error, and offer a final review page before submission.

Be transparent about status: every application shows its reference number in `font-mono` with a `copy-button`, the current stage in words, what happens next, the expected time, and who to contact. Never leave a person guessing.

Support many languages and reading directions from the start: text can grow 30 to 40 percent, names and addresses are not a US shape, dates and numbers follow the locale, and the language switcher is always visible and labeled in its own language.

No dark patterns: no pre-ticked consent, no countdown pressure on benefits, equal prominence for decline and accept. Ask only for data you need and explain why. Assume a poor connection and an old device: keep pages light, show upload progress, retry safely, and always offer a phone, paper or in-person alternative.

needs.need: Apply for a permit, licence or benefit (multi-step form)
needs.notes: `stepper` for stages, `field` for label, hint and linked error, `repeater-field` for household members or prior addresses.
needs.gap: No built-in save-and-resume or draft persistence (store drafts server side), no address lookup, and no check-your-answers summary page; build the review page from `table` or a definition list.

needs.notes: `dropzone` with per-file `progress`, accepted types and size shown in the hint, and a `badge` for Uploaded or Needs attention. Always keep a plain file-input path working.
needs.gap: No camera or document scan capture and no virus-scan or upload retry logic; those belong to your backend.

needs.notes: `stepper` for the stage, `timeline` for dated events (received, in review, more information needed, decided), `badge` with words for status, `alert` when action is needed from the applicant.
`auth-screen` for email and password; `otp-input` for SMS or authenticator codes, with a resend control and a non-SMS route.
needs.gap: No digital identity (eID, login.gov style) hand-off flow or knowledge-based verification; wire your identity provider and show its error states in `alert`.

needs.notes: Case queue in `table`, case file in `detail-page` with `tabs` for documents, notes and history, decisions through `approval-card`, and `timeline` as the case history.
needs.gap: `filter-table` is task shaped (todo, progress, done); use `table` with your own filters for case states. No assignment board with SLA timers.

needs.need: Book an appointment or inspection slot
needs.notes: `date-picker` plus a `radio-group` of times can cover a simple booking.
needs.gap: No calendar or availability grid showing open and booked slots, and no reschedule or cancel view.

needs.need: Pay a fee, fine or tax
needs.notes: `checkout` gives the details, payment and confirmation flow; show amount, due date and what it is for in `stat` and `table`; receipts via `order-confirmation`.
needs.gap: Payment methods and wording are retail shaped; relabel for a fine or fee and add instalment-plan and concession options yourself.

needs.need: Service notices, closures and emergency banners
needs.notes: A persistent, dismissible `alert` at the top for service disruption or deadlines; keep the same severity words across services.

needs.need: Find a service, office or document (search and directory)
needs.notes: `search-list` for live results, `accordion` for FAQs, `empty-state` for no results with a next step.
needs.gap: No map or location finder, and `catalog` is card shaped and retail oriented so use `search-list` for text-first service lists.

needs.need: Civic data and public dashboards (budgets, performance, open data)
needs.notes: Relabel `analytics-dashboard` for service volumes or spending, and always put a `table` next to each chart as the accessible alternative.
needs.gap: No general time-series, bar or map chart with text alternatives built in.

integrations.note: Keep all copy in message files, test with long German and Finnish strings, and set `dir` for right-to-left languages; check each opendraft component in RTL, since some spacing uses left and right classes.
Use `auth-screen` for the fallback email path and `otp-input` for codes, and show a clear error and recovery route when identity checks fail.
Automated tools catch only part of the problems; test each form with a keyboard and a screen reader, and test at 200 percent zoom.
Offer manual entry in a `field` group as the fallback and never block submission when lookup fails.
Pair with `dropzone` for intake; opendraft has no signature pad or PDF viewer, so use the provider's embedded signing and viewing.

integrations.for: Notifications by email, SMS and letter
integrations.note: Mirror each notification as a dated entry in `timeline` so a person can see what was sent without needing the message.

domains.title: Manufacturing and industrial operations
domains.summary: Manufacturing execution (MES), shop-floor terminals, quality control, maintenance and industrial IoT dashboards. Used by operators on a feet-and-gloves schedule and by engineers and managers reviewing lines, lots and downtime.
principles: Make state glanceable from across the room. Line, machine and order status uses large type, a word (Running, Idle, Down, Changeover) plus an icon, and high contrast; a wall display needs no reading beyond the status and one number.
Design for gloves and noise: touch targets of at least 56 px on shop-floor terminals, generous spacing, no hover-only or drag-only actions, and confirmations that do not rely on sound alone.

Every unit of product has traceability: lot, batch, serial, shift, operator and machine appear on the record, in `font-mono` with a `copy-button` and a scannable code, and corrections add a new entry rather than overwrite an old one.

Rank alarms by priority, not arrival time: Critical (stop and act), Warning (act this shift), Info. Keep alarm text specific (what, where, what to do), require acknowledgement with a name and time, and avoid alarm floods by grouping repeats.

Show shift and time context everywhere: the current shift, shift start, counts since shift start, and timestamps in the plant's local zone. Handovers between shifts need a visible notes and open-issues summary.
Tolerate offline and flaky networks: queue entries locally, show an explicit Saved locally, Syncing and Synced state, never lose a count or a quality reading, and show how stale a displayed value is.

needs.need: Line and machine status wall display (andon)
needs.notes: Large `stat` tiles for output, target and OEE with a `status-indicator` and status `badge` per machine; `progress` for output against target; `alert` for stoppages.
needs.gap: No large-format kiosk or full-screen display mode, and no auto-rotating screen layout; build it with a scaled container.

needs.need: Production order execution on a terminal
needs.notes: Work instructions as a vertical `stepper` or `todo-list`, `quantity-stepper` for good and scrap counts, `approval-card` to confirm completion.
needs.gap: Default control sizes are desktop sized; set larger button and stepper sizes through classes and verify 56 px targets. No barcode scan input or numeric keypad.

needs.notes: Inspection steps in `todo-list`, pass or fail in `radio-group`, defect photos in `dropzone`, sign-off in `approval-card`, and history in `records-table`.
needs.gap: No statistical process control chart (X-bar, control limits) and no measurement-instrument input.

needs.notes: Alarm list in `table` sorted by priority with a text `badge`, `selection-actions` for bulk acknowledge, `timeline` for the event history, `alert` for the active critical banner.
needs.gap: No alarm-shelving or suppression workflow and no audible alarm control; those are logic you build around `table`.

needs.notes: OEE, availability, performance and quality in `stat` and `progress`; downtime reasons in `table`; `analytics-dashboard` relabeled for machines.
needs.gap: No Pareto chart, no stacked shift-by-shift time-series chart, and the dashboard range tabs are fixed at 7, 30 and 90 days.

needs.need: Maintenance work orders and preventive schedules
needs.notes: Work orders in `table` and `detail-page`, checklists in `todo-list`, history in `timeline`.
needs.gap: No scheduler, calendar or Gantt for planned maintenance and no meter-based trigger view.

needs.notes: Search a lot with `command-palette`, show genealogy in `table`, record history in `timeline`, and print a label with `qr-code`.
needs.gap: No tree or graph view for forward and backward genealogy, and no barcode formats other than QR (Code 128, DataMatrix).

needs.notes: Current readings in `stat` and `table` with unit and last-update time.
needs.gap: No live time-series trend chart, no gauge or dial, and no P&ID or floor-plan view. `slider` and `switch` are fine for setpoints, but writes to a PLC need your own interlocks and confirmation.

needs.notes: Stock levels as `progress` with `invert` so low stock warns; handover notes in `textarea` and `timeline`.
needs.gap: No barcode scan input and no pick list or kanban board for material requests.

integrations.for: Machine and sensor data over industrial protocols
integrations.note: Bridge to the browser through a gateway or WebSocket and show the timestamp from the source, not the browser's receive time, so stale data is obvious.
Grafana panels can be embedded beside opendraft `stat` tiles; opendraft has no native time-series chart yet, so a library must draw trends.

integrations.for: Barcode and QR scanning on the floor
options: Hardware scanners that act as keyboards
integrations.note: Most scanners type into a focused field; keep one large focused `input` ready and show the scanned value back clearly. `qr-code` only renders codes.

integrations.for: ERP, MES and quality system connections
integrations.note: Keep the order, lot and BOM data read through your API and write corrections as new records, which matches the audit trail the UI shows.

integrations.for: Offline-first data and sync on terminals
integrations.note: Surface the Saved locally, Syncing and Synced state with a `badge` and use `sonner` only for failures that need action.
Render the on-screen label with `qr-code` and `font-mono` text, then send the matching ZPL to the printer.

domains.title: HR and people operations
domains.summary: HRIS, recruiting, onboarding, payroll, performance and time-off products used by employees, managers and HR teams. The data is personal and sensitive, so who can see what, and who changed what, is part of the design.
principles: Make views permission-aware: show each person only the fields their role allows, and say so (`Visible to HR only`) rather than leaving a blank. Managers see their reports, employees see themselves, and a view-as preview helps admins check it.

Mask sensitive data by default (salary, national ID, bank details, health and leave reasons, performance ratings) with an explicit reveal that is logged. Never put such values in URLs, toasts, page titles or exports without a clear warning.

Approval flows show the whole chain: who requested, who must approve now, who is next, what was decided and when. Give every request a status word (Pending, Approved, Declined, Withdrawn) and always allow the requester to withdraw or edit before a decision.

Use inclusive language and flexible data: do not require a binary gender field, allow preferred and legal names, support names that do not fit first and last, and keep pronouns optional. Dates, currencies and working weeks follow the person's country.

Make changes auditable: every edit to pay, title, manager, status or personal data records who, when, old value and new value, visible in a history view. Keep effective dates separate from edit dates so retroactive changes are clear.

Treat people-related decisions with care: show the reason and next step on rejections, avoid ranking people by a single score, label AI-generated summaries or suggestions as such, and keep a human decision-maker on hiring, pay and performance outcomes.

needs.notes: Searchable list with `avatar`, role and location, a profile in `detail-page`, jump-to-person with `command-palette`.
needs.gap: No org chart tree or reporting-line visualization.

needs.notes: Sections as `tabs`, editable details with `field`, a `dialog` to confirm reveal of masked values such as bank details.
needs.gap: No masked-field control with reveal and audit hook; build it from `input`, a toggle button and your permission check.

needs.notes: Request with `date-range-picker`, balance in `stat` and `progress`, decision with `approval-card`, approval chain in `timeline`.
needs.gap: No team calendar showing who is away and no public-holiday or half-day awareness; add holidays to the date picker logic.

needs.notes: `crm-pipeline` is a stage board with drag and drop; pass your hiring stages and relabel the cards; scorecards in `detail-page` with `tabs`.
needs.gap: Its data shape is sales oriented (company, value, contact), and there is no resume or PDF viewer. For fairness, hide fields (name, photo) you do not want in an early-stage blind review.

needs.notes: Steps in `stepper`, resume upload in `dropzone`, optional diversity questions as `radio-group` options that include Prefer not to say, and a confirmation screen via `order-confirmation`.
Tasks per owner (HR, IT, manager, employee) in `todo-list` or `task-rows`, overall `progress`, and sign-offs with `approval-card`.
Run stages in `stepper` (draft, review, approved, paid), differences against last run in `diff-table`, final approval via `approval-card`.
needs.gap: No payslip document viewer and no PDF viewer; link to a generated file. Calculation, tax and legal rules come from your payroll provider.

needs.notes: Review cycle in `stepper`, rating with `radio-group` that has a text label for each level, goals with `progress`, manager sign-off via `approval-card`.
needs.gap: No rich text editor for long-form feedback (`textarea` is plain) and no 9-box or calibration grid.

needs.notes: `timeline` for who changed what, `diff-table` for old and new values, `date-range-picker` and `table` filters for searching.

needs.need: HR analytics (headcount, attrition, time to hire)
needs.notes: Relabel `analytics-dashboard` for headcount and attrition; apply minimum group sizes so small teams cannot be identified.
needs.gap: No general time-series, funnel or cohort chart, and the dashboard range tabs are fixed at 7, 30 and 90 days.

integrations.note: Let the provider own the calculation and show its output in `table` and `stat`; never recompute pay in the browser.
Map their stages onto the `crm-pipeline` stages and keep candidate notes in your own detail view rather than copying them.

integrations.for: Single sign-on, provisioning and directory sync
integrations.note: Use SCIM to create and remove accounts at hire and exit, and drive the onboarding `todo-list` from the same events.
opendraft has no signature pad or PDF viewer; embed the provider's signing view and record the result in `timeline`.
Feed public holidays into the `date-range-picker` logic and sync approved leave to the team calendar.
Evaluate on the server and pass the allowed fields to the UI as props, so hidden data is never sent to the browser.

crossDomainGaps.title: Map and route view
crossDomainGaps.why: Fleet, flights, outages, assets, stores and attack paths all need a location view. Recommended base: MapLibre GL.

crossDomainGaps.title: Scheduler, calendar and Gantt
crossDomainGaps.why: Crew rosters, dispatch, appointments, timetables, shifts, maintenance windows and on-call.

crossDomainGaps.title: General time-series chart
crossDomainGaps.why: Several series, zoom, thresholds and gaps: metrics, energy, markets, vitals, SPC.

crossDomainGaps.title: Bulk-action bar for selected table rows
crossDomainGaps.why: Operators in logistics, security, HR and support act on many rows at once. Table gives selected IDs but there is no bar.

crossDomainGaps.title: Table that becomes a card list on phones
crossDomainGaps.why: Table scrolls sideways at 390px and hides columns; field, driver and patient screens need a mobile list.

crossDomainGaps.title: Signature pad and photo capture
crossDomainGaps.why: Proof of delivery, consent, field service and inspections.

crossDomainGaps.title: Rich text editor
crossDomainGaps.why: Notes, case files, content and messages. Recommended base: Tiptap.

crossDomainGaps.title: Date and time picker with time zones
crossDomainGaps.why: Aviation, logistics and scheduling must show and pick times in a named zone.

crossDomainGaps.title: ETA with confidence and staleness
crossDomainGaps.why: Logistics, aviation and field service need to show how sure an estimate is.

crossDomainGaps.title: Generic record detail page
crossDomainGaps.why: detail-page is shaped for buying a ticket; shipments, patients, cases, assets and employees need a record view with header facts, tabs and related items.

crossDomainGaps.title: Generic stage board
crossDomainGaps.why: crm-pipeline's data is sales-shaped; dispatch, hiring, cases and production boards need a neutral one.

crossDomainGaps.title: Video, PDF and document viewers
crossDomainGaps.why: Education, healthcare, legal and HR content.

crossDomainGaps.title: Gauge and risk-score ring
crossDomainGaps.why: Security posture, vitals, utilization and energy.

integrations.note: MapLibre is open source and needs no vendor key. A themed opendraft map wrapper is on the roadmap.
Read colors from CSS variables so charts follow the theme and dark mode; always offer a table alternative.

integrations.for: Data tables beyond a few thousand rows or with grouping
integrations.note: opendraft's Table is virtualized and covers most needs; reach for these for pivoting, grouping and column pinning.
Use the Field component for labels and errors, and let the schema produce the messages.
Style the editor surface with tokens and keep toolbars to the Button and Toggle patterns.
flowchart covers read-only flows; use these when users edit, pan and zoom.
Until opendraft has a scheduler, embed one and theme it with the CSS variables.
Mount the provider's hosted card fields in the checkout block's card slot so card data never touches your code.
Put the provider behind the auth-screen block; use otp-input for one-time codes.
Update rows in place and announce changes with an aria-live region.
qr-code only generates codes; scanning is a device capability.
Show documents inside a dialog or drawer so the surrounding screen keeps the theme.
